title: Chapter 89
content:
Jakyeong knocked twice and pushed the door open, only to freeze on the threshold.

The life-sized silicone replica that had been haunting the second-floor lounge was gone—transferred directly into Kang Il-hyun’s private master suite. While Jakyeong was staring at the uncanny effigy in utter disbelief, the en-suite bathroom door clicked open. Il-hyun stepped out, drying his damp dark hair with a towel slung around his shoulders, clad in nothing but a white terrycloth wrap around his waist.

With his fringe damp and the sharp edges of his face softened by the steam, the lethal, blood-drenched monster from the driveway had vanished without a trace.

Even after seeing the man stripped bare countless times, catching him half-naked still made Jakyeong’s ears burn. He quickly averted his eyes.

"I was planning on coming up to find you after I showered, but you couldn't wait to come down to me, could you, darling?"

Jakyeong’s brow pinched. "Chief Park said you called for me."

Whose version of the truth was real was anyone's guess, but seeing the teasing smirk on Il-hyun's face made the stoic security chief seem infinitely more reliable.

Without warning, Il-hyun unfastened the towel around his hips.

Jakyeong’s jaw dropped as the heavy, fully engorged erection sprang free, swaying rigidly in the open air. Twenty-four hours a day at full mast.

Utterly shameless, Il-hyun slipped into a silk charcoal bathrobe, loosely knotting the sash as he strolled over to the leather sectional. He sank onto the cushions and casually spread his knees wide, leaving the parted lapels teetering on the verge of total exposure.

Catching Jakyeong's trapped gaze, Il-hyun flashed an unvarnished, predatory grin.

"Unless you're planning to get on your knees and suck it, stop staring so hard."

The absolute audacity. If you sit completely bare with your legs spread wide open, where the hell else is a person supposed to look?

Jakyeong tossed a sofa cushion with homicidal intent, telling him to cover his damn crotch, but Il-hyun caught it effortlessly with a low chuckle. Left with no other choice, Jakyeong had to force his own eyes away.

Il-hyun sparked a flame to his cigarette, sliding a heavy kraft envelope across the coffee table.

Jakyeong picked it up, sorting through the contents: formal identity files, first-class boarding passes to Honolulu, and a business card accompanied by a surveillance-style headshot.

The departure date was stamped two days from now. In the photo, a man in a stiff black wool suit was posed against a sun-drenched Hawaiian beach—looking so severely out of place it resembled an amateur Photoshop job.

"Yoon Soo-hyun," Il-hyun said, blowing a thin stream of gray smoke. "He's the local handler assigned to take care of you on the ground. He'll receive you at Daniel K. Inouye International, so memorize the face."

The phrasing grated on Jakyeong's nerves. Take care of me? What am I, a toddler?

He threw an indignant glare across the table, but Il-hyun remained completely uncompromising—laying out a strict list of security protocols and repeatedly stressing that Jakyeong was under no circumstances to wander off alone.

Being ordered around before he had even formally agreed didn't sit well with him.

Noticing the dark cloud settling over the boy's brow, Il-hyun asked softly, "Don't want to go?"

"It's not that I don't want to..."

Jakyeong let his voice trail off.

His thoughts drifted back to the living room earlier. By the time he had showered and come downstairs, the two stone-faced assassins had already cleared out.

"Those two in the salon earlier."

"Yeah?"

"Are they new contractors you brought onto the payroll?"

Il-hyun gave a slight nod.

"Then isn't sending us away a waste of corporate capital? If you're going to pay top dollar just to bench me, why did you drag me back to Seoul in the first place?"

Snubbing out his cigarette in the crystal tray, Il-hyun smiled, a faint look of wounded fondness touching his dark eyes.

"Are you asking because you genuinely don't understand, darling... or are you playing coy?"

Jakyeong swallowed, his throat tightening.

Do you actually have feelings for me? You keep me around not just because my body is convenient in bed, but because you genuinely care?

A hundred unspoken questions piled behind his teeth. Ever since that sudden, irrational urge to protect this man had taken root in his chest, doubt had plagued his mind. Could a monster who openly despises and hunts his own biological family truly harbor genuine affection for another human being?

Then again, Jakyeong was hardly an authority on love. He had never truly loved anyone either—merely reaching out for fleeting warmth whenever the crushing isolation became unbearable. Which was why Wang Ryun’s weeping, inconsolable grief over a traitorous lover felt entirely incomprehensible.

"If you have something on your chest, spit it out," Il-hyun coaxed, sensing the heavy gears turning behind the boy's dark eyes.

Jakyeong clamped his lips shut and shook his head, sliding the travel documents back into the envelope. Nothing would change by overthinking it. The man was his primary employer; his job was simply to execute the brief.

"Are they reliable?" Jakyeong asked, needing to confirm the operational baseline. "Those two?"

Il-hyun smiled, pushing off the sofa to slide onto the cushion right beside Jakyeong. A faint, sweet trace of peach blossoms from the body wash drifted off his skin. It seemed entirely mismatched with a syndicate heir, yet Jakyeong found himself leaning in slightly, catching the scent.

Il-hyun wrapped a long arm around Jakyeong's shoulders, hauling him tight against his chest. When Jakyeong made a half-hearted attempt to pull back, Il-hyun caught his hand, threading their fingers together with a soft interlock before tilting his chin up to meet his gaze.

Strangely enough, simple, domestic intimacies like this felt infinitely more flustering to Jakyeong than raw, bruising sex.

When Jakyeong looked away in embarrassment, Il-hyun rested his cheek against the boy's shoulder. It didn't cost anything to let him lean, so Jakyeong let him be.

"Don't tell me... you're actually worried about my safety?"

"As if."

"They might not shoot as straight as you, darling, but their acting skills certainly blow yours out of the water."

Jakyeong scowled, shoving him back by the collar. "Drop the snark."

Losing his temper only provoked the beast—Il-hyun lunged forward, tackling Jakyeong flat onto the cushions. Through the thin silk robe, the rock-hard, burning length of his erection pressed flush against Jakyeong’s thigh.

Jakyeong thrashed to throw him off, but the sheer difference in mass pinned him down completely.

"Hey! Get off!"

"Say it nicely," Il-hyun purred against his jaw. "'Please get off me, President Kang.'"

Jakyeong ground his molars together, spitting each syllable through clenched teeth:

"Please. Get. Off."

Il-hyun beamed, answering without a beat:

"No."

Jakyeong closed his eyes in pure exhaustion, seriously debating whether to break the man's nose again before boarding the flight.

Before he could throw a strike, Il-hyun shifted, sliding onto the sofa behind him. The leather sectional was generous, but accommodating two grown men lying down was an intimate squeeze.

Wrapping both arms around Jakyeong’s waist, Il-hyun pulled the boy flush against his front, wedging them tightly against the backrest.

Through the thin cotton of his shirt, the heavy, rhythmic thud of Il-hyun's heartbeat pulsed against his spine. When Jakyeong shifted to make space, the arms around his ribs only tightened their possessive lock.

The master suite fell into a tomb-like hush. Lying bracketed against that towering chest brought a strange, disorienting warmth.

Il-hyun slipped his forearm beneath Jakyeong’s neck, offering a soft pillow of muscle, and gently patted his shoulder.

"I'll sing you to sleep."

When Jakyeong snapped that he didn't need a babysitter, Il-hyun began humming a low, wordless melody beneath his breath. When Jakyeong asked what song it was, the man admitted with a chuckle that he was making it up as he went.

Come to think of it, Jakyeong had never in his life had someone sing him a proper lullaby.

"Did anyone ever sing to you when you were little?"

"Never. I've slept alone in a locked room since I was an infant."

"Weren't you scared?"

"Of what?"

"Ghosts... the dark..."

"There's no such thing as ghosts."

Jakyeong blinked. Once, while holed up in a dilapidated safehouse hotel in the Philippines with Wang Han, he had witnessed a white, translucent apparition dart across the hallway. Just recalling the memory sent a chill down his neck.

"They're real. I've seen one."

Il-hyun let out a quiet scoff. "A professional assassin who believes in ghosts... What a tragic waste of nerve."

When he puts it like that, it does sound pretty ridiculous. Jakyeong felt a faint sting of embarrassment.

"What else terrifies you besides spirits?"

Jakyeong considered the question. Cockroaches, centipedes, and anything possessing more than six legs—which was why he had an affinity for serpents, since they had none. The recurring nightmares of his dead parents rising from the dirt to choke the life out of him... and aside from that, nothing really came to mind.

"Tell me about when you were little," Il-hyun whispered softly, his fingers absentmindedly playing with the shell of Jakyeong’s ear. "I want to know."

It was the very first time the man had ever asked about his childhood. When Jakyeong offered no answer, the long fingers continued their gentle, rhythmic caress.

It wasn't a past he ever wanted to drag into the light. The endless beatings, running drop-packages for street dealers, chewing on cardboard to stave off starvation, and getting beaten half to death again... It was a waking nightmare so relentless that, even as a ten-year-old child, he had prayed for a bullet just to end the misery.

His dark eyes glazed over, fixed on the empty floorboards. Whenever his memory drifted back to those alleys, his brain felt as though it were freezing in ice.

"You don't have to talk about it if you don't want to."

Uncharacteristically, Il-hyun backed off without pressing.

The fingers drifting from his ear moved to gently stroke his dark hair. The steady, tender cadence was overwhelmingly soothing, dragging a heavy, irresistible drowsiness over his eyelids. The cramped leather sofa felt unexpectedly warm, his consciousness slipping beneath the surface with every passing breath.

He made a weak attempt to push himself up toward his own room, but the hold tightened.

"M' sleepy..." Jakyeong mumbled.

"Sleep right here. I'll carry you to the bed later."

A faint, drowsy smirk touched Jakyeong's lips. "What am I, a princess?"

"Who says the prince is the only one allowed to do the carrying? If it pleases you, darling, I'll gladly play the princess."

The teasing tone was soft and velvety.

As Jakyeong’s eyes fluttered shut, the low, wordless humming resumed, the deep resonance in Il-hyun's chest vibrating against his spine like a gentle balm.

Jakyeong stirred in the dark, blinking against the gloom.

Heavy blackout drapes sealed the master suite in near-total darkness. Reaching out across the mattress, the sheets beside him were cool and empty. He reached up, flicking on the low-wattage nightstand lamp to survey the room.

He remembered being lifted and carried into the bed in a half-dream, but Il-hyun was gone.

Sliding off the mattress, he noticed the travel envelope resting on the nightstand.

Opening the bedroom door, he spotted a tall silhouette standing motionless before the floor-to-ceiling glass in the private salon.

Holding a crystal tumbler of scotch, Il-hyun was staring out into the pre-dawn mist. His sharp profile looked terrifyingly cold beneath the pale, bruised blue of the morning sky—radiating the lethal, calculated stillness of an apex predator waiting to break from the treeline.

Hearing the soft rustle of footsteps, the icy detachment instantly melted from his features, replaced by a bright, effortless smile.

"Awake already?"

On the low table sat an empty bottle of single malt. Did he finish that entire fifth by himself? Yet his balance and speech were impeccably sharp.

"Have you been drinking out here all night?"

"Yeah. Couldn't sleep."

Jakyeong walked over, plucked the crystal tumbler straight from Il-hyun's grip, and brought it to his lips, knocking back two heavy, burning swallows of amber liquor before Il-hyun snatched the glass back.

"Stop that. Your drunken brawls are bad for my health."

"..."

"Though I must admit... your jealous rage was quite flattering."

Jakyeong glared over the rim. He had protested a dozen times that he hadn't thrown a fit out of jealousy, but the man stubbornly refused to hear it.

Turning from the window, Il-hyun pinned his undivided attention onto Jakyeong's face. The cold, boardroom calculations had vanished, replaced by an intoxicating cocktail of unmasked affection and raw hunger.

Il-hyun stepped forward, eliminating the space between them. Jakyeong didn't retreat an inch.

Long, warm fingers grazed across Jakyeong's lips, slowly parting them to slip inside.

"Suck."

Jakyeong hesitated for a fraction of a second before extending his tongue, tracing the pads of the fingers sliding over his teeth. It wasn't the two sips of scotch making his head spin, yet his body obeyed the command without resistance.

Il-hyun smiled, stepping flush against him until their chests collided, his lips brushing the shell of Jakyeong’s ear in a low, intoxicating rasp:

"Watching you sleep so peacefully... I nearly lost my mind wanting to tear you apart."
